name: layout19
description: Adaptive Korean soft-girl multi-UI editorial collage — layering multiple digital interface fragments over a dreamy atmospheric background. Before composing this layout, analyze the first uploaded image and extract three things: (1) dominant color palette — identify the 2–3 hero colors and 1–2 accent tones present in the outfit; (2) outfit aesthetic/mood — classify the overall vibe (e.g. soft feminine/lace, Y2K baddie, preppy campus, dark academic, streetwear, cottagecore, etc.); (3) outfit motif or texture — identify any recurring pattern or material quality (lace, ruffle, gingham, leather, solid jersey, floral print, etc.). Color rule: all UI chrome tones, decorative element colors, chat bubble tints, sidebar icon colors, and overlay accents must use a complementary or contrasting palette relative to the outfit's dominant color — not the same hue (e.g. cream/blush outfit → soft sage green or dusty periwinkle UI accents; navy outfit → warm peach or amber; white outfit → muted lavender or forest green). Complementary contrast should feel dreamy and editorial — soft tonal opposites, not saturated clashes. Background is a full-bleed soft atmospheric image (blurred cherry blossom canopy, soft bokeh garden, or equivalent nature/environment scene) in tones from the complementary palette, pushed to very low opacity/saturation so it reads as a dreamy canvas; if no nature setting fits the aesthetic, use a muted solid in a complementary tone with fine grain. UI layer system — stack multiple interface fragments across the canvas, all styled in complementary neutral tones: (1) simulated web breadcrumb navigation bar at top (e.g. 'My Account > Posts > Today') as a pill-shaped rounded bar; (2) monthly calendar grid ghosted across upper background at low opacity, date numbers visible; (3) social media action sidebar on right edge — vertical stack of icon buttons (heart, search, profile, link, share) in a rounded pill container, colored in the complementary accent; (4) ghost keyboard row (partial, Q W E R T Y etc.) at very low opacity across lower background. Photo slots: one medium portrait card upper-left (thin border or borderless, slight tilt), one medium portrait card upper-right (straight, thin border), one small portrait card mid-left (borderless, overlapping calendar grid), one large hero close-up portrait lower-right as dominant anchor (no border, full presence); if 5–6 photos available, add one extra small card in the center or lower-left gap. Decorative graphic elements: derive element types from the aesthetic mood of the first uploaded image (e.g. soft feminine lace/ruffle → heart charm keychain cutout, illustrated drink cup cutout, small flower hair-clip cutout, paper receipt or café bill scrap; Y2K baddie → scattered fruit or candy cutout, paper airplane, vintage clock; streetwear → bold label stickers, chain hardware, spray-texture marks; cottagecore → pressed botanical cutouts, ribbon bow, woven texture swatch) — but render all element colors in the complementary/contrasting palette, not the outfit's own colors. Stacked iMessage-style chat bubbles (receive side) in lower-left with 2–3 short affirming or mood-matching phrases — bubble color from the complementary palette. Cursive or brush-script name/title signature in complementary tone at lower-right. Small sparkle star (✦) stickers scattered at 3–5 points in complementary accent color. All cutout and overlay colors must stay within the complementary color story. Soft daylight or studio photography, clean and airy. Follow the multi-UI-layer stack with scattered card arrangement; adapt slot count within the 4–6 range.
swipe_cta: Add a small swipe CTA element styled as one of the UI fragments already present in the layout (e.g. breadcrumb nav continuation '→ Next', small rounded pill button 'Swipe →', or chat bubble 'see more ♡'). Color it in the complementary/contrasting palette relative to the outfit — not the outfit's own hue. Keep wording minimal (2–4 words). Position near the bottom edge, integrated naturally with the UI layer stack.
